subject: general
question: Which Indian state celebrates Makar Sankranti as 'Poush Sankranti'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Poush Sankranti or Poush Parbon**, a well-known event, is widely observed in **West Bengal**.
 
• In Bengal, Poush Sankranti is a lucky day when farmers begin **harvesting their crops.**
 
• Rice grains are used in** Lakshmi Puja **rituals as a symbol of the goddess of wealth.
 
• The holiday is also known as **pithe parbon**, and the most popular delicacy for celebration is called **pithe** made from rice flowers.
 
• West Bengal
 
 
• **Chief minister:** Mamata Banerjee
 
• **Capital:** Kolkata
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maharashtra:**

 
 
• ​Makar Sankranti is observed as **Maghi Sankrant or Haldi Kumkum** in Maharashtra and Goa.
 
 
 
• **Himachal Pradesh:**
 
 
• ​Locals in Himachal Pradesh observe **Magha Saaji **as Makar Sankranti.
 
• **Sankranti **is known locally as** Saaji,** and the month is called **Magha.**
 
• People visit the temples on this day to seek the Lord's blessings and take a plunge in the area's sacred rivers.
 
 
 
• **Rajasthan:**
 
 
• "Makar Sankrati" is also known as** "Sakraat"** in the Rajasthan.
 
• It is specifically observed in** Jaipur** as a **kite-flying competition** amongst several groups.
 
• **Rajasthani specialties and sweets** including pheeni, til-patti, gajak, kheer, ghevar, pakodi, puwa, and til-laddoo are served to mark the day.
 
 

1b
